sections.text: O Arjuna! I rescue them from the ocean of life and death, for their minds are fixed on Me.
मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय।
Then let thy mind cling only to Me, let thy intellect abide in Me; and without doubt thou shalt live hereafter in Me alone.
अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम्।
But if thou canst not fix thy mind firmly on Me, then, My beloved friend, try to do so by constant practice.

What is my purpose and destiny? So far we had been discussing the bhakti yoga chapter 12, and there are 20 verses in this chapter. Its a pretty small chapter because there is not much to tell you. Everything that has to be told is already told in the chapters before.
So as we have discussed, from chapter six to ten we saw the Bhagavans Vibhuti, his glory, his identification, how to find him in this manifest world. We saw in chapters 6 to 10 where he said, I am in the fragrance of flower, I am the sweetness of honey, I am even in the cheating power of the cheats. Whatever you can think of is the essence of a thing or a being.
The dharma of that being or a thing is me. A thing only exists because of its inherent quality to be its own Dharma. We are human beings because we have the basic qualities necessary for a human being.
You take that away, you are no more a human being. If a person looks like Michael Jackson, you go near, but he doesnt move, we know its just a Madame Tussauds Museum statue. Thats not Michael Jackson.
Because that statue does not have the inherent qualities required to be Michael Jackson. So that which makes you you, and I I, and it it -- Bhagavan said -- is me. We have seen that from chapter six to ten, and from that we should have developed a devotion to the Lord.
But obviously thats not that simple. So Arjuna asked Bhagavan in chapter 11, I understood all of it, but I want to experience it -- I cant experience it. So with Lords grace, he gets a divine vision to comprehend this oneness in this manifest world, which is what we had been talking about. We just cant connect with that on our own.
And Arjuna gets connected to that where he sees this manifest world as nothing but one being with many mouths, many hands, many legs, and many things happening. With that understanding, one should develop the devotion to that being, that one supreme Being who is nothing but my own self. So chapter 12 is the yoga of devotion.
Once you contemplated who I am, realize the nature of the supreme and realize that myself and the supreme selves are not two different selves. I must instantaneously develop identification with that supreme self, which we call it a love for the Divine devotion. So this chapter is about all the Bhakti Yoga, how to unite with yourself by devotion.
And we had been talking about various paths to attain that oneness with the Supreme. And we have talked about three different three distinct paths. Karma Yoga, Bhakti Yoga, Gnana Yoga.
And we always get confused because of our cultural baggage. We have understood bhakti as something which happens in a temple or during bhajan time. Im not that kind of bhakta. I dont really wear a mala and keep doing kirtan all day.
Im not a bhakta like that. So here is our chance to understand what bhakti really is. So the chapter opened with Arjunas two obvious questions. Should I be devoted to you in the form which I have seen -- you as Krishna or Rama or Shiva, Jesus, whatever -- whom I have now recognized as divine, while Im a mortal, and put my faith into that one manifestation to achieve oneness? Or, as others discussed in the Vedas and Upanishads, should I worship that being which is Nirguna, Nirakara -- no qualities, no shape and form -- that all-pervading being in its unmanifest form? And obviously Bhagavans answer was: one who gives his mind to me and has me as the supreme goal and does it with faith, he comes to me quicker.
But the others who want to devote to the unmanifest, if they can do the following -- Samniyamya indriyagramam, all the senses under control, equanimous to all, where they can see the equanimity in this entire manifest world, where they can see that underlying thread in this world of plurality and diversity which binds this entire universe -- that thread which we already discussed in previous verses. Sutre eva, Maniganaha eva -- just as a thread in a necklace of beads -- we can see that underlying unity. And then, Sarvabhutahite rataha, Im constantly engaging myself in the welfare of all beings.
Not just my group of people, my family, my people -- while other people can go wherever -- but Sarvabhuta hite rataha, the welfare of all. Then he also comes to me, Bhagavan said. And then obviously the question is, which one is better? Should I devote to a particular deity whom I feel closest to and most inspired by? And Bhagavan said, both are fine.
But Kleso adhikatarasteham -- those who devote to the unmanifest, its a harder path. There are more obstacles on the way. For Dehavadbhih, those who are attached to the body, the first qualification required is to have Samniyamya indriyagramam -- all the senses under control.
But if Im not at that level and still have attachment to these senses and the body, no matter how intellectually I consider myself non-dualistic, that attachment to duality will bring me down. And therefore Bhagavan says for them it is more difficult if you are Dehavadbhih. Not just the indweller of the body, but one who is attached to this body.
I never understood the meaning of samadhi -- they talk about it in meditation and all this. But one time Tejomayanda explained it to me in one simple term. He was not addressing just me, but an audience.
But I got it. He said, You are in a state of samadhi all the time -- a samadhi with reference to your body. There is never a time where I am not identified with my body. Nobody has to wake me up and say, Rajan, thats not you, thats you. Im always in a state of samadhi with reference to my body.
Thats actually Dehavadbhih. Im attached to this body. For me, clinging to this body as the ego-I and then trying to establish myself into the supreme unmanifest -- Bhagavan says Kleso adhikatarasteham, for them there are lots of difficulties.
Therefore he said, the easy path is Mayyeva mana adhatsva. Give your mind to me and then do everything for me. And I will become your savior -- to save you from this ocean of samsara, this ocean of experiences which seems infinite.
I dont see the end of it. So many times I thought I got it. We told Bhagavan, Oh Lord, just give me this, just give me a green card and Ill be fine. Oh Lord, give me a green card.
Because the green card these days takes about eight to ten years. I have somebody with me who has been here like six years now. I applied for his green card about three years ago, and we are renewing for the third time.
So believe it or not, his prayer to the Lord is what? Oh Lord, give me a green card. After that Im taken care of, right? Green card lets you stay here, do whatever you want to do. And as soon as you get the green card -- what? Oh Lord, find me the right partner. So now I can settle down. And then it continues.
Many, many times we thought there was an end to these difficulties, that once I get past this sorrow Ill be done. But the moment we get there we realize, no, no -- the infinite experiences which give me joys and sorrows never end. It never comes with pure joy.
What I really want to achieve is a state where there is no sorrow. But this Samsara -- Samsarati -- the constantly changing life of mine, these infinite experiences, I dont see the end of it. One thing ends, a new thing starts.
Bhagavan says, for those who have given their mind to me and have supreme faith in me, I become their savior. They are not capable by themselves of crossing this ocean of infinite experiences -- infinite experiences in a finite world. I will be the savior for them, to save them and take them to the other side.
Where there is no sorrow, where there is pure happiness -- what you are looking for. There is no ignorance about who I am, there is no death, there is no end of me. There is no ignorance and there is no sorrow.
So its all about the mind -- thats what we figured out. Bhagavan never said give me your intellect and body. The intellect is nothing but a memory bank of my experiences; I think I know based on only my experiences.
But the mind takes flight into the unknown and keeps on going. There is a story about a Sankalpa Shali -- one who cant control his imagination. Id heard a story in my childhood about a Brahmins son who makes his living by getting bhiksha, alms.
One day he got more bhiksha than he could consume. He said, Well, today was a good day and I got a lot of this bhiksha. I cannot consume all of it. So what Im going to do is take the part which is left and sell it and make some money.
Then what Im going to do with that money? Well, Ill buy this and then Ill do this little business. Then Ill make more money, and then I will find a worthy partner. Then Ill get married. And then I will have children, and then children will come to me. And in his excitement he kicked -- he kicked that pot which had the flour in it, broke it, and it was all gone.
His flight of imagination took him away, and he lost everything he was dreaming about. So Bhagavan said, that quality of the mind which we have seen is Sankalpa Shakti. You need to curb that and put it in me.
Nivasishyasi mayyeva ata urdhvam na samshayah. Fix thy mind in me, place thy intellect in me too. See, right now we are so dependent on our own intellect.
Doubt comes to the mind. Almost everybody who learned Bhagavad Gita has said, All this is great, but I dont think you can succeed if you just continue like this. You have to have passion and drive, then only you can succeed in life. So learn this, but dont get hung up on it. Why? Because we are relying on our own intellect, which is nothing but a bank of finite experiences that tells us what succeeds and what doesnt.
We have seen people like Steve Jobs and say, Thats why they are succeeding -- I should be like that. Bhagavan said, no, dont rely on your intellect. It will misguide you, because it does not have the capacity to go beyond the realm of your experiences. What you are trying to cross is the realm of your experiences.
How can you rely on your intellect for that? You need to plug into the global database, the cosmic database. If I dont know anything, what do I do? I go on Google and see if I can find it. If I find it on Google, Im fine.
That entire database of the supreme intellect, that cosmic intelligence, I need to rest in that. I have to rest my intellect into that. Plug into not only my hard drive which is my intellect to the cloud computing connected to that Bhagavan.
Not only give your mind to me but rest your intellect into me. Realize that there is a guide who will guide me once I put faith in him.

Krishnas promise in verse 7 is breathtaking: I rescue them from the ocean of life and death (mrityu-samsara-sagarat). The image of samsara as an ocean is powerful, endless waves of experience, joy and sorrow rising and falling, with no shore in sight. We have all felt this: the moment we achieve one goal, another desire arises. Green card leads to wanting a partner; partnership leads to wanting children; children bring new anxieties. The cycle seems infinite. Yet Krishna offers Himself as the rescuer for those whose minds are fixed on Me (mayy-avesita-cetasam).
The practical instruction in verse 8 is remarkably direct: Let thy mind cling only to Me, let thy intellect abide in Me. This is not passive wishing but active engagement. The mind must be placed (adhatsva) in the Divine; the intellect must be established (nivesaya) there. As the teaching explains, our intellect is like a personal hard drive with limited data from our finite experiences. Devotion means plugging into the cosmic database, trusting a wisdom greater than our own accumulated knowledge. When doubt arises about decisions, ask: Am I relying solely on my limited experience, or am I open to guidance from a higher intelligence?
Verse 9 offers compassionate encouragement for those who struggle: If thou canst not fix thy mind firmly on Me, then try to do so by constant practice (abhyasa-yogena). This is the path for most of us. Practice today by setting three reminders on your phone. When each reminder sounds, pause whatever you are doing and consciously place your attention on the Divine for just one minute. Notice how the mind resists, wanders, returns. This is abhyasa yoga, patient, persistent practice without expectation of immediate perfection.
